cases.title: An option after a known wrapper verb as a bytes constant leaves every key equal
cases.given: A scratch copy of skills/sdlc and hooks at 39aa68f; push_guard.py clean output as the baseline
cases.when: A bytes option is added after fetch: b"--upload-pack=git push origin sdlc/S-001-v0-cli-0;:" in a state-write.py git call, the same in a next-action.py run call, and b"-u" in a state-write.py git call
cases.expected: Each form changes wrapperVerbs, opaque or pushes

seeds.title: push_guard.py reads every non-str constant as constant text
seeds.detail: pieces() returns str(node.value) for any Constant, so b"--upload-pack=..." folds to the token b'--upload-pack=... with no leading dash. value_nodes() skips it as constant. A bytes option after the verb records no wrapperVerbs entry. A bytes argument before the verb is read as the verb, which breaks the pin only by chance. A fix can treat a bytes constant (or any non-str constant) as non-constant, or record it as a value entry.

seeds.title: suite-receipt.py git wrapper raises TypeError on a bytes argument
seeds.detail: The error message joins args with ' '.join, so a bytes argument raises TypeError after the git call ran. Not a defect today, since no caller passes bytes.
